extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalism students, practicing journalists, and general readers interested in news media
extracted.subtask_description: Sociological analysis of how major U.S. newsrooms choose national stories — examining the values, professional standards, external pressures, and organizational structures that shape news judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values influencing news selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'values' that shape journalists' judgments about which stories to cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gans spent ten years observing journalists to identify the values that inform news selection. The page emphasizes these values as a core factor shaping news judgment, noting they persist even as media change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'professional standards' to which journalists adhere when choosing and producing news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book examines newsroom professional standards as a determinant of story selection and presentation. It treats these standards as part of the internal norms guiding reporters and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: External pressures shaping journalists' judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'external pressures' (e.g., political, economic, social) that influence which stories are chosen and how they are framed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gans analyzes how outside forces exert pressure on newsroom decision-making. The page references these pressures generally (without enumerating types) as a major influence alongside values and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of national stories that inform a nation's self-understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of national news stories that 'inform America about itself' — i.e., the societal role of news in reflecting national events and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description frames the target of selection as national stories that shape public understanding; this provides an evaluative lens for what counts as important news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness of headline events
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to prioritize major headline events (e.g., War on Poverty, the Vietnam War and protests, urban ghetto disorders, assassinations, Watergate) as newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists historical headline events included in Gans's study as examples of the sorts of occurrences newsrooms selected. These serve as exemplars of newsworthy subject matter in the book's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structures and routines of news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The internal 'structures of news organizations' (routines, hierarchies, institutional arrangements) that shape news judgment and selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gans's account emphasizes how newsroom structures and routines influence decisions; the page notes that 'the basics of news judgment and the structures of news organizations have changed little,' implying institutional continuity as an evaluative factor.
